# #3468: Patch: follow-up to #3467 from the after-merge spot-check
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

<!-- jackioh-bot:spot-check-follow-up #3467 -->
The after-merge spot-check of #3467 ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/42582126293)) found 3 blocking problem(s) in the change as it merged (`e8d5f21f9b55`). `claude-3` (claude, `opus`, strong) reviewed it. #3467 stays merged: nothing is reverted, and this issue fixes what it found in a change of its own, from `main`.

## What to fix

- [ ] `apps/web/src/fx/shed.ts:16`: The shed level is one module-wide global with no production reset, so after a game sheds to stage 3 every card face in the app stays still (except a hovered one) until some fx director happens to run about 90 healthy frames of effect work; outside a game no director ever runs, so faces stay still for the rest of the session.
  Evidence: The only writes to the level are `setShedLevel` in director.ts:225 (a slow window) and director.ts:235 (recovery); `resetShedForTests` is the only reset. `dispose()` (director.ts:698-705) does not touch it. `adapt` is called only from `onFrame` (director.ts:598), and the loop sleeps when `hasWork()` is false, so an idle board never recovers. `useMotionSlot` (cards/motionSlots.ts:104-105) reads the global for every face, through `useArtMotion` (cards/cosmetics.ts:700), and that hook runs in CardFace.tsx:417, which renders faces across the whole client, not only the board. PackOpening.tsx:157, StatShowcase.tsx:174 and routes/dev/fx.tsx:173 create their own directors, and those write the same global. Nothing limits shedding to a phone either: three stalls of more than ~720 ms (FX_ADAPT_WINDOW 30 × FX_ADAPT_SLOW_MS 24) on a desktop also freeze it. Fix: reset the level when a director is disposed (or keep it per director), let an idle board recover, and decide on a phone-only gate.
- [ ] `apps/web/src/fx/aura/AuraLayer.tsx:131`: AuraLayer subscribes to the shed pointer at every stage, so every pointermove re-renders it, and each render runs measureAll (getBoundingClientRect on every aura zone, a forced layout) plus drift.sync and wake. That is a new per-move layout cost on the board, desktop included, at stage 0 where the pointer is never used.
  Evidence: `const pointer = useSyncExternalStore(subscribeShed, shedPointer, ...)` is read on every render. FxLayer.tsx:349-357 calls `setShedPointer` on every window pointermove, and shed.ts:63-68 notifies on every changed position. The layout effect at AuraLayer.tsx:191-194 measures after every render (its own comment says so), and the effect at ~271-282 re-syncs the drift engine. `budgetFor` only reads the pointer when `shedAuraScale(shed) !== 1`. The new scenario's own tilt circling (startTilt) fires a pointermove every frame, so it also measures this cost. Fix: read the pointer only at stage 2 or deeper (for example, subscribe to the pointer only when shed ≥ SHED_AURAS), or test boxes against the pointer without making the pointer render state.
- [ ] `apps/web/src/fx/constants.ts:251`: The issue asks for one shared phone budget that faces, tile auras, backdrops, particles and tilt draw from. PHONE_MOTION_BUDGET is never read by any code, and nothing counts those units against it. The ruling describes behavior the code does not have.
  Evidence: grep for PHONE_MOTION_BUDGET in apps/ and e2e/ finds only its definition, a comment in shed.ts:2 and constants.test.ts, which checks only that it equals COSMETIC_FOIL_ANIMATED_MAX. R3351000.md says the units 'share six concurrent motion units: a face counts 1, an aura 1, tilt 1'. In practice the six face slots are the existing motion slots, and the tile auras, backdrop and tilt run on top of them with no count and no shedding triggered by a count. The scenario board alone has 5 tile auras, field auras, a backdrop and a tilted card besides the faces. Either enforce the shared count (faces + auras + tilt ≤ PHONE_MOTION_BUDGET on a phone, shedding in the ruled order) or reword the ruling and the constant to say what the code actually does.

## Done when

- Each finding above is fixed where it points, or answered with the evidence that it does not hold.
- Every check is green, with no test skipped, ignored or weakened to get there (CLAUDE.md rule 12).
